body.statement: Using the branch-dual saddle handle in \(\text{def:full-class-handle}\), characterize \[\sup_{D\in\mathfrak D_2^{\mathrm{all}}}\inf_{\mu:\,|\arg\max_i\mu_i|=1}\frac{\Gamma_D(\mu)}{I_w(\mu)}.\] Is its value \(G\), so that the proportional schedule is already optimal, or can a nonproportional first-stage or survivor allocation achieve a strictly larger certified multiplier? Derive an attaining design and a matching saddle certificate in either case.
body.justification: The unrestricted multi-survivor two-batch frontier is the genuine open content beyond the exact proportional top-\(m\) theorem.
body.gap: Existing batch-complexity results use different fixed-budget or fixed-confidence criteria; no cited theorem gives the joint heteroskedastic robust-gain saddle value over survivor count, first-stage allocation, and branch-specific survivor allocations.
body.consumer: A solution determines whether experimental platforms lose any worst-instance exponent by enforcing the proportional survivor-allocation interface and its certified discrete survivor-count choice.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove or refute \(\sup_{D\in\mathfrak D_2^{\mathrm{all,multi}}}\inf_{\mu:\,|\arg\max_i\mu_i|=1}\Gamma_D(\mu)/I_w(\mu)=G_{\mathrm{multi}}\), and exhibit an attaining design with a matching saddle certificate.
obligation.obstruction: The finite quadratic branch programs are explicit for each fixed design, but arbitrary first-stage and branch-specific survivor allocations couple the least-favorable mean across all retained-set branches.  The frozen results provide no allocation-uniform dual witness and no minimax interchange over the open simplices and the discrete choice of \(m\).
obligation.attempted: Used \(a=w\) and \(b_{J,i}=w_i/W_J\) to embed every proportional top-\(m\) design and obtain the lower bound \(G_{\mathrm{multi}}\).  Also substituted general \(a\) and \(b_J\) into the Gaussian polyhedral branch programs.  Optimizing a witness separately for each branch does not furnish a single mean vector adversarial for the full branch minimum.
